steps.heading: Windows over time
steps.body: rolling(n) looks at a fixed-size trailing window of n rows; expanding() grows from the start of the series, never resetting. Both need an aggregation (.mean(), .sum(), .std()...) to actually produce a value.

steps.heading: A moving average
steps.caption: The first window_size - 1 rows are NaN — there's no full window yet.

steps.heading: Comparing to earlier rows
steps.body: shift() lines up a value from n rows away against the current row. diff() and pct_change() are shorthand for the absolute and relative change against the previous row. cumsum()/cummax() accumulate from the very start, with no window at all.

steps.heading: Day-over-day change
steps.caption: You'll practice rolling, expanding, shift, diff, pct_change, cumulative functions, and ewm in the cards that follow.
